### CVE-2025-1217 — Header parser of http stream wrapper does not handle folded headers
- Assigner: php | Published: 2025-03-29 | Updated: 2025-11-03 | Max CVSS: 6.3
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/AU:Y/R:A`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

In PHP from 8.1.* before 8.1.32, from 8.2.* before 8.2.28, from 8.3.* before 8.3.19, from 8.4.* before 8.4.5, when http request module parses HTTP response obtained from a server, folded headers are parsed incorrectly, which may lead to misinterpreting the response and using incorrect headers, MIME types, etc.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.* <8.1.32 (semver); affected 8.2.* <8.2.28 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.19 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.5 (semver)

Credits: Tim Düsterhus

References:
- https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-v8xr-gpvj-cx9g
- https://security.netapp.com/advisory/ntap-20250523-0008/
- https://lists.debian.org/debian-lts-announce/2025/03/msg00014.html

### CVE-2025-1219 — libxml streams use wrong content-type header when requesting a redirected resource
- Assigner: php | Published: 2025-03-30 | Updated: 2025-11-03 | Max CVSS: 6.3
- CWE: CWE-1116 CWE-1116 Inaccurate Comments
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

In PHP from 8.1.* before 8.1.32, from 8.2.* before 8.2.28, from 8.3.* before 8.3.19, from 8.4.* before 8.4.5, when requesting a HTTP resource using the DOM or SimpleXML extensions, the wrong content-type header is used to determine the charset when the requested resource performs a redirect. This may cause the resulting document to be parsed incorrectly or bypass validations.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.* <8.1.32 (semver); affected 8.2.* <8.2.28 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.19 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.5 (semver)

Credits: Tim Düsterhus

References:
- https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-p3x9-6h7p-cgfc
- https://security.netapp.com/advisory/ntap-20250523-0007/
- https://lists.debian.org/debian-lts-announce/2025/03/msg00014.html

### CVE-2025-1220 — Null byte termination in hostnames
- Assigner: php | Published: 2025-07-13 | Updated: 2025-11-04 | Max CVSS: 3.7
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 3.7 LOW `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

In PHP versions:8.1.* before 8.1.33, 8.2.* before 8.2.29, 8.3.* before 8.3.23, 8.4.* before 8.4.10 some functions like fsockopen() lack validation that the hostname supplied does not contain null characters. This may lead to other functions like parse_url() treat the hostname in different way, thus opening way to security problems if the user code implements access checks before access using such functions.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.* <8.1.33 (semver); affected 8.2.* <8.2.29 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.23 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.10 (semver)

Credits: Jihwan Kim

References:
- https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-3cr5-j632-f35r
- https://lists.debian.org/debian-lts-announce/2025/07/msg00017.html
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2025/07/11/4

### CVE-2025-6491 — NULL Pointer Dereference in PHP SOAP Extension via Large XML Namespace Prefix
- Assigner: php | Published: 2025-07-13 | Updated: 2025-11-04 | Max CVSS: 5.9
- CWE: CWE-476 CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 5.9 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

In PHP versions:8.1.* before 8.1.33, 8.2.* before 8.2.29, 8.3.* before 8.3.23, 8.4.* before 8.4.10 when parsing XML data in SOAP extensions, overly large (>2Gb) XML namespace prefix may lead to null pointer dereference. This may lead to crashes and affect the availability of the target server.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.* <8.1.33 (semver); affected 8.2.* <8.2.29 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.23 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.10 (semver)

In PHP versions:8.1.* before 8.1.34, 8.2.* before 8.2.30, 8.3.* before 8.3.29, 8.4.* before 8.4.16, 8.5.* before 8.5.1, the getimagesize() function may leak uninitialized heap memory into the APPn segments (e.g., APP1) when reading images in multi-chunk mode (such as via php://filter). This occurs due to a bug in php_read_stream_all_chunks() that overwrites the buffer without advancing the pointer, leaving tail bytes uninitialized. ### CVE-2025-14179 — SQL injection in pdo_firebird via NUL bytes in quoted strings
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-05-10 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-89 CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'); CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P/AU:Y/RE:M/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

In PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.31, 8.3.* before 8.3.31, 8.4.* before 8.4.21, and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, the PDO Firebird driver improperly handles NUL bytes when preparing SQL queries. During token-by-token query construction, a string token containing a NUL byte is copied via strncat(), which stops at the NUL byte, dropping the closing quote and causing subsequent SQL tokens to be interpreted as part of the string. This allows SQL injection when attacker-controlled values are quoted via PDO::quote() and embedded in SQL statements.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.31 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.31 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.21 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.6 (semver)

### CVE-2025-14181 — Integer overflow to buffer overflow in soap HTTP parsing
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-09-25 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 6.5
- CWE: CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer overflow or wraparound
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 6.5 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

The SOAP HTTP client guards its response buffer growth with a check that relies on signed integer overflow, which is undefined behaviour and is not guaranteed to trigger. When the check is optimised away, a malicious SOAP server can make the client allocate a buffer far smaller than the data it then writes into it, producing a heap buffer overflow.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.34 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.35 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.26 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.11 (semver)

### CVE-2025-47275 — Brute Force Authentication Tags of CookieStore Sessions in Auth0-PHP SDK
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2025-05-15 | Updated: 2025-05-22 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287: Improper Authentication
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Auth0-PHP provides the PHP SDK for Auth0 Authentication and Management APIs. Starting in version 8.0.0-BETA1 and prior to version 8.14.0, session cookies of applications using the Auth0-PHP SDK configured with CookieStore have authentication tags that can be brute forced, which may result in unauthorized access. Certain pre-conditions are required to be vulnerable to this issue: Applications using the Auth0-PHP SDK, or the Auth0/symfony, Auth0/laravel-auth0, and Auth0/wordpress SDKs that rely on the Auth0-PHP SDK; and session storage configured with CookieStore. Upgrade Auth0/Auth0-PHP to v8.14.0 to receive a patch. As an additional precautionary measure, rotating cookie encryption keys is recommended. Note that once updated, any previous session cookies will be rejected.

Affected:
- auth0 / auth0-PHP: affected >= 8.0.0-BETA1, < 8.14.0

Auth0-PHP is a PHP SDK for Auth0 Authentication and Management APIs. Versions 8.0.0-BETA3 prior to 8.3.1 contain a vulnerability due to insecure deserialization of cookie data. If exploited, since SDKs process cookie content without prior authentication, a threat actor could send a specially crafted cookie containing malicious serialized data. Applications using the Auth0-PHP SDK are affected, as are applications using the Auth0/symfony, Auth0/laravel-auth0, or Auth0/wordpress SDKs, because those SDKsrely on the Auth0-PHP SDK versions from 8.0.0-BETA3 until 8.14.0. Version 8.3.1 contains a patch for the issue.

Affected:
- auth0 / auth0-PHP: affected >= 8.0.0-BETA3, < 8.3.1
